issue.title: Datapath tap for a USB network path: filtered RX copy and best-effort TX injection, no AVTP stream frames
issue.body:
## Objective

Give the USB audio device's FX3 a network path (kebag-logic/usb-audio, CDC-ECM network function). Tap the Milan MAC with a filtered RX copy toward a GPIF thread, and inject the computer's frames on TX into the best-effort queue. A controller on the attached computer then sees and controls the network, while AVTP stream frames never reach USB.

## Owner decisions (2026-11-25)

- The computer is its own station, with a locally administered MAC that the FX3 regenerates at every USB connection and hands to the FPGA.
- No gPTP/MSRP mirroring: control only.

## Scope

**RX filter (MAC to GPIF thread).** Copy a frame toward the computer when:
- its destination is the computer's MAC; or
- it is broadcast or multicast, excluding AVTP stream subtypes (AAF, CRF and the other stream formats) and 802.1 link-local destinations 01-80-C2-00-00-0x.

The device's own reception is unchanged. Unicast to the device's MAC stays with the device.

**TX inject (GPIF thread to MAC).**
- Inject only into the best-effort queue, below the SR classes. Credit-based shaping and class A/B must be unaffected.
- Apply a rate limit.
- Drop any frame with an AVTP stream subtype or a link-local destination.
- Drop any frame whose source is not the computer's MAC.

**Interface.** A frame FIFO with length headers on two GPIF threads. A register for the computer's MAC, written by the FX3.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Verilator tests:**
   - every filter class, with a planted defect for each;
   - the TX drops;
   - the best-effort-only injection;
   - with injected traffic at its rate limit, the SR class A/B shaping is unchanged in the existing harness.
2. **Routed totals** within the agreed band for the Mark II USB image (expected ~1-2k LUT, 1-2 BRAM, to be measured), and timing at every corner.
3. **Bench:** a controller on the computer works while the device's streams run concurrently with clean counters.

Not before the 2026-11-30 lab-ready target. Refs https://github.com/kebag-logic/usb-audio/issues/5.

comments.body:
[A10] Added requirement: **audio has priority over the network function on every shared link.**

- **Ethernet:** the computer's frames go into the best-effort queue only, which is strict priority below SR classes A and B under credit-based shaping (IEEE 802.1Q-2018, 8.6.8 and 34). This is already in milan-fpga#1011.
- **USB:** audio uses isochronous endpoints, whose bandwidth USB 3 reserves; CDC-ECM uses bulk endpoints, which get the remainder. This comes from the protocol.
- **GPIF bus (FPGA master to FX3):** the audio and network threads share one 16-bit bus, so the FPGA master's arbiter serves the audio threads first and on schedule. The network threads get only leftover cycles, with a capped share.

New acceptance criterion: with the network path saturated in both directions, the audio streams keep every counter clean: no FX3 underrun or overrun, no late or early samples, and no USB isochronous errors.

[A10] **Rulings on PR #1020's open questions.**

1. **A local path both ways is required.**
   - The device's own transmitted frames must also reach the computer under the same receive-copy rule: unicast to the computer, broadcast and multicast, without AVTP stream subtypes or link-local destinations.
   - The computer's frames addressed to the device, and its broadcast and multicast frames, must reach the device's own receiver, as frames from the network do.
   - Without both directions the computer cannot discover or control this device, and that is the purpose of the function.
2. **The 01-80-C2-00-00-2x block (MVRP, MMRP) is excluded, like the -0x block, and transmitted frames tagged above priority 1 are dropped.** Both are accepted. They keep the path to control only.
3. **The station record's format is the one the FX3 side fixes** in kebag-logic/usb-audio PR #7, `docs/NETWORK.md`; see the amendment above. The FPGA side adopts it in its next round: the MAC, the USB state LD1 reads, and the detach.
4. **GPIF threads:** a third address line on the harness, waiting for the owner's answer. The FPGA side stays thread-agnostic.

pr.body:
The USB network path copies permitted frames and injects rate-limited best-effort traffic while preserving endpoint priority. Arty status LEDs follow the [fabric-level ruling](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/1020#issuecomment-7213370880): LD2 means any media-locked input or open output transmit gate; LD3 means internal selection or a locked selected source. The control image contains no LED register or LED handling.

The [held-egress ruling](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/1020#issuecomment-7234489667) gives USB-network Arty its own ledger point under #894's rule. Each row uses the larger original Arty or injected measurement. The table is in `docs/design/USB_NET_PATH.md`; only its last AECP figure differs, at 62.14 ms. The original Arty and 8x8/1if ledgers remain unchanged. These remain seven recorded service-budget misses, bounded by their separate ledger.

All 159 retained traces across eight images regrade identically. Qualification passes at the USB point with no new or larger miss. The unchanged owner row gives load 0.501397, ACMP 29.84 ms, txL 48.90 ms and last notice 117.58 ms. The retained complete wire result is 644.981 us against 1000 us. Controls preserve the 62.03635-versus-61.99 rejection at the original Arty point and reject one cycle over 62.14 at the USB point. All 25 ledger mutations are detected; final documentation and inventory gates pass. Inventory regeneration is a separate commit.

Firmware, RTL, the queue model and scheduling costs are unchanged. The Arty and both ALINX control ELF/map-header comparisons remain byte-identical to #1004's same-pin builds. The other thirteen dependency files are unchanged. Previous simulation, filter and LED plants, injection controls and shaping evidence retain their exact inputs.

Board observations, attachment integration, physical-route qualification, broader candidate gates and independent review remain open. Existing whole-image crossing and external-I/O limitations remain. No physical release or issue completion is claimed.

## Scope and authorities

Read AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/README.md, the issue bodies and public scope rulings, REQUIREMENTS.md (especially REQ-CSR-03, REQ-CBS-*, REQ-CLS-03/06/09 and REQ-VER-*), the register/interface and reset contracts, then the diff/history, then the public author receipts. - [Issue #1011](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/1011): filtered receive copy, checked best-effort injection, rate limit, unchanged SR shaping, routed cost/timing, and physical concurrent-stream acceptance.
- [Station-record amendment](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/1011#issuecomment-7186353239) and [scope rulings](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/1011#issuecomment-7188062527): local forwarding in BOTH directions is required; the -2x destination exclusion and PCP > 1 rejection are accepted; the FX3 document owns the forthcoming record format.
- [Issue #1018](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/1018): LD0 activity/link, LD1 working SuperSpeed path, LD2 connected streams, LD3 selected-clock satisfaction, AECP selection tests and board observations.
- [FX3 NETWORK.md at its published head](https://github.com/kebag-logic/usb-audio/blob/ca34e0d2272eb14e126f8f6d67a98ee596057ff6/docs/NETWORK.md): two-word length/kind header and 16-byte station payload. - [Published author evidence](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/tree/7ca25ea258496fab3ab73d76b7c7138cb503c1f4/review-evidence/usbnet-r1/author) is source execution evidence. No manager source bank exists or is claimed here.

## Findings

### R950-1-01 - MAJOR - Conformance, RTL, Robustness, Tests

**Artifact:** `hdl/usbnet/KL_usbnet_tx_inject.sv:314`, `:340`, `:345`; `tb/verilator/usbnet/sim_main.cpp:507`; receipt `rate-hold.log` and reproducer `rate_hold_probe.cpp`.

**Authority/evidence:** #1011 requires a rate limit. `docs/design/USB_NET_PATH.md:105` defines a wire-octet token bucket with a 3,200-octet burst. `start_w` spends tokens when preparing an output frame, independently of arbitration or acceptance. While that frame waits, the bucket refills to its full capacity. The pending, already-paid frame then leaves in addition to the full bucket.

The exact-head tap, using its existing 1 MHz / 800 kb/s test parameters, was given four 1,000-octet frames with injection disabled. After the pending frame's tokens refilled, injection was enabled. First-beat times were 1, 1605, 3210 and 4814 clocks after enabling. The fourth frame brings the wire charge to 4,096 octets; the allowed envelope is only 3,681.4 octets. Even at the fourth frame's simulated wire completion, after 6415 clocks, the completed 4096 octets exceed the 3841.5-octet envelope. Both independent assertions fail (exit 1). A blocked arbitration grant has the same accounting mechanism. The ordinary steady-rate suite and all existing rate plants pass, so they do not detect this defect.

**Impact:** releasing a held injection permits more than the advertised burst, by as much as one previously reserved frame's cost. This does not demonstrate changed CBS arithmetic or loss of datapath priority; it demonstrates that the output traffic fails its stated limiter envelope.

**Required outcome:** account for a pending frame so the actual injection stream obeys the specified rate/burst envelope after arbitrary grant or downstream waits. Preserve full-frame, gapless transmission and datapath priority.

**Verification:** add an independently calculated cumulative wire-octet envelope check after a long disabled-injection interval, arbitration delay and MAC backpressure, using short and maximum-size frames. It must fail this head and pass the correction, alongside the existing rate and priority suites.

### R950-1-02 - MINOR - Tests

**Artifact:** `tb/verilator/usbnet/sim_main.cpp:218`, `:306`; `hdl/usbnet/KL_usbnet_rx_copy.sv:236`; receipts `last-plant.log`, `last-plant.rc`; reproducer `run_last_probe.py`.

**Authority/evidence:** the bus contract in `docs/design/USB_NET_PATH.md:150` requires `last` on each record's final word so the transfer can be committed. The harness captures only `up_data_o` and reconstructs records from lengths. It never observes `up_last_o`. A disposable plant replacing the receive block's final-word marker with constant zero passes all nine cases, including “records toward the computer are well formed”, with exit 0.

**Impact:** a broken transfer-commit marker can pass the current tests while preventing the receiving bus adapter from committing valid transfers. The unmodified RTL does produce the marker; this is a demonstrated verification hole, not a claim that the present marker logic is broken.

**Required outcome:** independently grade exactly one accepted terminator per record, precisely on its final word, including odd lengths and stalled final words; grade marker stability while stalled.

**Verification:** the constant-zero plant and premature/extra-marker plants must fail their dedicated checks; the original exact-length streams must pass.

### R950-1-03 - MINOR - Conformance, RTL, Robustness, Tests, Docs

**Artifact:** `docs/design/USB_NET_PATH.md:137`; `hdl/usbnet/KL_usbnet_rx_copy.sv:45`; `hdl/usbnet/KL_usbnet_tap.sv:105`; receipts `rx-length.log`, `rx-length.rc`; reproducer `rx_length_probe.cpp`.

**Authority/evidence:** the current FPGA bus-record table specifies FRAME lengths 14 through 1518 in BOTH directions. The integrated receiver instead uses the default `MAX_LEN_P=2000`. An exact-head probe presents broadcast frames of 1518, 1519, 2000 and 2001 octets: the first three produce records with those respective lengths; only 2001 is dropped. The current receive tests stop at 1514 and do not compare the upper boundary to the stated interface contract.

**Impact:** a consumer implementing the documented record limit can receive an out-of-contract record. This is a mismatch inside the present FPGA contract, separate from the already acknowledged adoption of the FX3 format next round. It is not pure prose residue because the disputed text specifies an interface length and the observable output violates it.

**Required outcome:** make the integrated receive limit and the authoritative direction-specific record limits agree, consistently with the approved downstream contract. Do not silently enlarge a consumer's accepted range.

**Verification:** test maximum-minus-one, maximum and maximum-plus-one in both directions, checking output bytes, length, verdict, terminator and recovery of the following valid frame. Reconcile the document and integration parameter with those results.

## Applied lenses and executable evidence

**Conformance:** examined the complete `KL_usbnet_pkg.sv` rules against #1011 and its amendments: host/other unicast, broadcast/multicast, both reserved destination blocks, AVTP subtype bit 7, both recognised VLAN tags, stacked-tag rejection, source identity and PCP 0/1 versus higher priorities. Inspected the corresponding 26 RX classes (attached and detached), 21 TX cases and unknown-record recovery. Findings 01 and 03 leave this lens unclean. The local path and station-record adoption are explicitly pending scope.

**RTL:** examined all six added RTL files and `sw/litex/usbnet_soc.py`, plus each changed SoC hook. Traced speculative FIFO rollback/commit, whole-frame admission, synchronous reads, last-byte conversion, strict priority after `tx_sf`, outstanding datapath-frame accounting and request/ack crossings. Compared the substituted frame-end toggle to `docs/design/REBOOT_RESET.md` and the gPTP destination observer. Reviewed the input register added in the final commit against the preceding version. The same-clock observer never drives RX backpressure. The existing shaper and queue sources are unchanged. Findings 01 and 03 leave this lens unclean.

**Robustness:** examined malformed/short/stacked-tag handling, unknown records, invalid station addresses, detach/stale host records, FIFO full/drop/rollback, odd-byte padding, stalled injection, token replenishment, link-down activity and reset domains. Existing full-buffer, contention, stalled-MAC and detach cases pass. Added held-injection and receive-size boundary probes fail as recorded above. No exhaustive reset-phase sweep or physical clock-loss test was run. Findings 01 and 03 leave this lens unclean.

**Tests:** independently executed the two exact-head RTL baseline harnesses; all 43 named RTL plants were detected. Independently executed the unchanged CBS, shaping-core and queue suites: all pass. Executed the four firmware LED tests on the shipping configuration and every checked-in Arty model (`arty_4x4`, `arty_8ch`, `arty_current`), and all eight LED plants: all detected by their specified assertions. Inspected `test_aecp.cpp:294` onward: all three LD3 cases invoke SET_CLOCK_SOURCE and check the descriptor update; locks and binding come from explicit mocks. Traced those observations into `ctrl_app_aecp.c`, `aecp_face.c` and the fabric counters; these unit cases are not a real MMIO/board demonstration. Findings 01, 02 and 03 leave this lens unclean.

**Docs:** compared the new design page, source port comments, CSR placement and firmware map generation against the implementation and public scope decisions. Reviewed the public receipt index, gate results, ALINX identity, firmware identity, CSR row diff, route recipe, timing extracts, utilisation and hierarchy. No new prohibited lane/review marker was found in added source comments. The receive-size contract mismatch is substantive (03). Impact: a consumer implementing the documented record limit can receive an out-of-contract record. This is a mismatch inside the present FPGA contract, separate from the already acknowledged adoption of the FX3 format next round. It is not pure prose residue because the disputed text specifies an interface length and the observable output violates it.

Required outcome: make the integrated receive limit and the authoritative direction-specific record limits agree, consistently with the approved downstream contract. Do not silently enlarge a consumer's accepted range.

Verification: test maximum-minus-one, maximum and maximum-plus-one in both directions, checking output bytes, length, verdict, terminator and recovery of the following valid frame. Reconcile the document and integration parameter with those results.

Existing full-buffer, contention, stalled-MAC and detach cases pass. Added held-injection and receive-size boundary probes fail as recorded above. # R949-1: internal independent review of PR #1020 (#1011, #1018)

- **Round.** R949-1, internal cleared-context reviewer.
- **Head.** `cc49123d2db1e01e80859efa10f8da43a01344ef`, tree `0ffb57980a908eb6b330ce5968a9a6bc8c690496` (verified in the clone).
- **Base.** Source base `c34e7d8b06739a22cc79997a9a1f4cbcd9bd0350` (dev-soft-core), 8 commits, 22 files, +3004/-12.
- **Reconstructed from.** AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md; docs/README.md; #1011 body and its three owner-side comments (7165838061, the 7186353239 interface amendment, the 7188062527 rulings); #1018 body; the diff and history; the author's evidence packet `review-evidence/usbnet-r1/author` at 7ca25ea2; the hosted check runs at the head.
- **Not read.** No private author material and no other reviewer's report was read before this verdict.
- **Verdict.** NEGATIVE.
  - One BLOCKER: the new suite breaks the mandatory Verilator sweep and its CI shard selection.
  - One MAJOR: after a reset of the system-clock side alone, injection never resumes, and the module header says that reset is harmless.
  - Three MINOR findings, one RESIDUE and two SUGGESTIONs.
  - All five lenses were applied and all five are UNCLEAN at this head.

## Findings

### F1 BLOCKER - Tests, Docs - `tb/verilator/usbnet/` against `scripts/suite_shards.py:80` (SUITE_SECONDS) and `scripts/suite_tally.py` - the new suite is not wired into the sweep, so the sweep fails
- **Authority.**
  - The `suite_shards.py` docstring: "New suites must enter both the discovered inventory and duration table".
  - The `suite_tally.py` NOCOUNT rule: "A suite that measured nothing is an UNKNOWN ... It fails the sweep".
  - CONTRIBUTING section 2.1 step 7 and section 3 make `scripts/run_all_suites.sh` mandatory.
  - AGENTS section 7 requires exact-head `verilator-suites`.
- **Evidence at the head.**
  - `python3 scripts/suite_shards.py --suite-root tb/verilator --ci-pieces --shard 0/27` exits rc 2 with "usbnet: inventory suite with no recorded duration in SUITE_SECONDS" (`receipts/suite_shards_shard0.txt`).
  - `suite_shards.py --selftest` reports `FAIL head: usbnet: ...` and "selftest: 1 FAILURE(S)", rc 1 (`receipts/suite_shards_selftest.txt`).
  - At base c34e7d8b both pass, rc 0 (`receipts/suite_shards_base.txt`), so the failure comes from this change.
  - `run_all_suites.sh:342` aborts on that self-test before running any suite. `rtl.yml:336` and `:596` run the same self-test in the hosted jobs.
  - The suite also prints no tally line in a shape `suite_tally.py` reads ("PASS: 0 failure(s)", "PASS leds: 0 failure(s)"). `suite_tally.py` on its log gives `NOCOUNT usbnet`, ACCOUNTING FAILURE, rc 1 (`receipts/suite_tally_usbnet.txt`). `run_all_suites.sh:502` then exits 90.
  - The suite index (`tb/verilator/README.md`, `docs/testing/TESTING.md`) does not list `usbnet`.
- **Impact.** Neither the mandatory local sweep nor the required hosted `verilator-suites` context can pass at this head. The new checks are never tallied.
- **Required outcome.**
  - `usbnet` is registered in SUITE_SECONDS following the docstring's new-suite steps, with the shard budget re-checked.
  - Both harnesses print a recognised tally shape.
  - The suite appears in the suite index.
- **Verification.**
  - `suite_shards.py --selftest` PASS.
  - The `--ci-pieces` selection exits rc 0.
  - `suite_tally.py` on the usbnet log shows no NOCOUNT.
  - `run_all_suites.sh` and hosted `verilator-suites` pass at the new head.

### F2 MAJOR - RTL, Robustness, Tests, Docs - `hdl/usbnet/KL_usbnet_tx_arb.sv:34-40`, `:96-97`, `:133-137`, `:166-173` - injection stops for good after a reset of the system-clock side alone
- **Mechanism.**
  - The grant needs `out_r == 0 && answered_w`.
  - Suppose the system side is reset after an odd number of granted injections, all answered. `req_r` goes back to 0, but the transmit side's `ack_r` stays 1.
  - The next datapath frame end is then taken as an answer and not toggled. `out_r` counts that frame in but never out, so it stays one high.
  - `grant_lo_w` never holds again.
- **Probe** (`scripts/probe_reset_cases.cpp`, `scripts/build_probe.sh`; `receipts/probe_arb_reset.log`). After a system-side reset following 1 injection:
  - 0 of 3 later computer frames are injected (`tx_passed_o`=3, `tx_injected_o`=0);
  - 3 of 4 datapath frame ends are counted.
  - Controls: after 2 injections, or with both sides reset, 3 of 3 frames are injected and 4 of 4 ends are counted.
- **Authority.**
  - The module's own RESETS paragraph says such a reset "only lengthens the reboot wait to its bound". That is false.
  - AGENTS section 6, Robustness: "reset during activity".
  - CONTRIBUTING section 1 reset rules.
  - No harness case resets either side alone: the bench resets both together, and only at construction.
- **Reachability.**
  - In the product, the `macsys` reset is `sys.rst | reinit`.
  - The link guard raises `eth_rst` together with `reinit`. Both sides are therefore reset, and the counters agree again provided the transmit clock runs (`milan_soc.py:1795-1867`).
  - A system reset during which the transmit side's synchronous reset sees no clock edge reaches the defect. So does any later reset of one side alone.
- **Impact.** The computer's transmit direction stops silently and permanently: frames are counted as passed but never sent, until both sides are reset. The documented reset contract is wrong.
- **Required outcome.**
  - A reset of either side alone leaves the arbiter able to grant again: request and acknowledge resynchronised, or a bounded recovery.
  - The RESETS text states the real behaviour.
  - A harness case resets each side alone during activity, after both odd and even grant counts, with a planted defect it catches.
- **Verification.** The probe's three cases pass, and the new case catches its planted defect.

### F3 MINOR - Conformance, Docs, Tests - `hdl/usbnet/KL_usbnet_rx_copy.sv:45` (`MAX_LEN_P = 2000`, not overridden in `KL_usbnet_tap.sv:102`) against `docs/design/USB_NET_PATH.md:137` - receive records are longer than the bus contract allows
- **Authority.** The page says a FRAME record is "14 to 1518" octets in both directions, and calls itself "the contract the USB device firmware works to".
- **Probe** (`scripts/probe_rx_length_cases.cpp`; `receipts/probe_rx_length.log`). Received broadcasts of 1519, 1600 and 2000 octets are copied with exactly those record lengths. A 2001-octet frame is refused (RXV_SHAPE). The harness's longest RX case is 1514.
- **Impact.** A USB device firmware sized to the documented 1518 limit receives longer records.
- **Required outcome.** The RTL and the contract agree, either by bounding the copy and counting the refusal, or by documenting 2000 with its reason. The boundary is tested.
- **Verification.** The probe at 1518 and 1519 behaves as the chosen contract says, and a planted defect at the bound is caught.

### F4 MINOR - Tests, Docs - stated rules with no test and no planted defect
- **(a) RX length rule.** The length half of RX rule 2 (`KL_usbnet_pkg.sv:122`, `len < need_octets(h)`) can be removed and the harness still passes (`probe_rx_length_rule_removed` survives).
- **(b) TX header-length rule.** The TX header-length rule for frames tagged under 19 octets or AVTP under 15 (`KL_usbnet_pkg.sv:134`) can be removed and the harness still passes (`probe_tx_length_rule_removed` survives).
- **(c) LD3 EXTERNAL rule.**
  - The firmware rule at `sw/firmware/ctrl/plat/ctrl_plat_leds.h:119` is `kind == CTRL_PLAT_LEDS_EXTERNAL && domain_locked`.
  - With the domain lock dropped, `Leds.*` still passes 4 of 4 (`receipts/probe_fw_external.txt`).
  - No checked-in model has an EXTERNAL clock source.
- **Evidence.** `receipts/mutants_parallel.txt` for (a) and (b); the probe was planted, run and restored for (c).
- **Authority.**
  - `USB_NET_PATH.md:236-237` and `:241-242` claim "one per rule".
  - #1011 AC1 asks for a planted defect per filter class.
  - #1018 AC1: "Each rule has a planted defect".
- **Impact.** Breaking these rules goes undetected. A short frame's verdict could be decided by header octets left over from an earlier frame. An unlocked EXTERNAL source would light LD3.
- **Required outcome.** Each rule has a test and a planted defect: short RX and TX frames for each header shape, and an EXTERNAL source in the `Leds` fixture. Otherwise the rule is removed or publicly declared out of scope, and "one per rule" is made true.
- **Verification.** The three reviewer probes fail their named checks.

### F5 MINOR - Docs - `docs/design/REBOOT_RESET.md:104-107` - the authoritative REBOOT page describes the old toggle
- **The page says.** `MilanMAC` flips `ethtxend_tgl` "on the last octet of every frame at LiteEth's `phy.sink`".
- **At this head.** With `--usb-net`, `KL_usbnet_tx_arb` produces the toggle and leaves the computer's frames out of it (`sw/litex/milan_soc.py:1837-1841`, `USB_NET_PATH.md:110-115`). The REBOOT authority was not updated.
- **Impact.** A cold reader of the REBOOT account gets the toggle's source and meaning wrong for the Arty `--usb-net` image.
- **Required outcome.** REBOOT_RESET.md states the `--usb-net` variant or links to USB_NET_PATH.md section 3.
- **Verification.** The doc diff.

### R1 RESIDUE - Docs - `hdl/usbnet/KL_status_leds.sv:40` - port comment names the wrong reset domain
- **The defect.** The `clk_i` comment reads "the system clock, the MAC wrapper's". The block is instantiated on `ClockSignal("sys")` with `ResetSignal("sys")` (`sw/litex/usbnet_soc.py:169`), not in the MAC wrapper's `macsys` domain.
- **Exact fix.** `//! the SoC system clock`.

### S1 SUGGESTION - Conformance - #1011 AC1d disposition
- **The criterion.** AC1d asks that SR class A/B shaping be "unchanged in the existing harness" with injection at its rate limit.
- **Why that harness cannot carry injection.**
  - The product TX trunk has no CBS (`hdl/milan/milan_datapath.sv:826-842`).
  - None of the inputs of the stand-alone `cbs`, `shaper_core` or `queues` suites changed. They pass at the head (`receipts/shaper_suites_head.log`).
- **What does measure it.** The tap harness measures the bound that matters: the worst datapath wait is 2314 or 2337 clocks, against a bound of one injected frame.
- **Suggestion.** Record publicly that this mapping is how AC1d is satisfied, so the frozen criterion is not reinterpreted privately.

### S2 SUGGESTION - Robustness - `hdl/usbnet/KL_usbnet_tx_inject.sv:174-179`, `:241` - HOST and DETACH records can wait behind a stalled frame
- **The behaviour.** A FRAME header waiting for room in P_ROOM holds the HOST and DETACH records behind it.
- **When it shows.** With `inject_en_i` low (internal loopback), or with injection starved:
  - the bus stalls;
  - LD1's freshness lapses;
  - a DETACH is not seen.
- **Suggestion.** Document this, or let host records bypass waiting frames.

### Open scope (not graded as defects, per the #1011 rulings)
- The local path both ways (ruling 1) is not in this head.
- The station-record format is to follow the FX3 side's `docs/NETWORK.md` (amendment and ruling 3).
- The GPIF thread assignment (ruling 4) is undecided.
- Bench items #1011 AC3 and #1018 AC4 are not done.

## What was checked in each lens

### Conformance (applied; UNCLEAN by F3)
Checked and found correct:
- **Stream subtypes.** The bit-7 stream rule matches IEEE 1722-2016 Table 6, with NTSCF, ESCF and EECF passing as control.
- **Link-local destinations.** The excluded 01-80-C2-00-00-0x block and the 2x block (ruling 2) are both implemented (`KL_usbnet_pkg.sv:92-127`).

- **ALINX identity.**
  - By construction: `usb_net_clk_hz is None` and `board == "arty"` guard every change in `milan_soc.py`, and `ctrl_plat_gen.py:162-163` emits `CTRL_PLAT_LEDS` only when the SoC's map has the row.
  - The author's identity receipts agree.
- **CSR map.** Rows are only added. The pinned page `n_locs - 5` is free, since the other pins are `-1` to `-4`.
- **Cost and timing.** +1221 LUT and +2 RAMB36 is inside the "~1-2k LUT, 1-2 BRAM" band, with every corner met (author receipts). The tap's FF count rises from 717 to 791, which equals the 74-bit input register of cc49123d. That supports the claim that the route carried this head's RTL.

### RTL (applied; UNCLEAN by F2)

### Robustness (applied; UNCLEAN by F2)
Checked and found correct:

### Tests (applied; UNCLEAN by F1, F2, F3, F4)

  - the tap suite passes 9 cases (799973 b/s; worst waits 2314 and 2337 clocks);
  - the LED suite passes.

- **Firmware LED defect rows.** All 8 apply exactly once (`receipts/fw_led_rows_applicability.txt`). Their campaign was not re-run.

### Docs (applied; UNCLEAN by F1, F2, F3, F4, F5)

- **Repository gates.** `docs_check.py`, `lint_rtl.py --check`, the SV, Python and C++ idiom gates and the port-contract gate all exit rc 0 (`receipts/gates_head_reviewer.txt`).

5. **Re-measure.** Regrade the retained 159 traces only.
6. **STOP** if a row exceeds its figure, a new miss appears, an owner bound fails, or firmware, RTL or the queue model changes.
